mainTopic: Challenges to, and support for, the rule that עצרת (שבועות) has make-up days (תשלומין) for its offerings, and whether work is allowed on those days.
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier answer with a פסוק: a person leaves ירושלים only in the morning. The גמרא then tests the rule of רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא that עצרת has make-up days (תשלומין) for its offerings. The first challenge comes from a משנה where בית הלל say that עצרת falling on Friday has 'no יום טבוח'. The גמרא answers that this only means no extra day is needed, and it shows why that dispute had to be taught alongside another משנה. A second challenge, from a source that mentions only 'the first יום טוב of עצרת', is answered by reading it as 'days of slaughter'. A third challenge compares עצרת to ראש חודש, which is one day. רבא rejects it, because עצרת is counted in weeks and is even called 'חג שבועות'. The גמרא then brings a teaching from the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: since reaping is forbidden on יום טוב, the 'festival when you reap' must mean the make-up days of עצרת. Finally it explains that this teaching adds something to רבי אלעזר's source: work is allowed on עצרת's make-up days, unlike פסח's. The reverse side of that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A verse: you leave in the morning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer with a פסוק: 'And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an answer that started before this section. The גמרא brings a פסוק to show that a person leaves ירושלים only in the morning, after staying the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in the morning' teach that you may not head home right after the offerings. You stay in ירושלים overnight and leave the next morning. That פסוק is the source that backs up the earlier answer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall turn (go back) in the morning'
'to your tents', meaning to your home

phrases.english: As it is written: "And you shall turn in the morning
and go to your tents."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer from before this section by giving its source פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That a person leaves ירושלים only in the morning, after staying overnight.

steps.title: Challenge: does עצרת have no make-up day at all?
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that when עצרת falls on Friday, בית הלל hold it has 'no יום טבוח'. The גמרא asks whether that means עצרת has no make-up days at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: if עצרת falls on ערב שבת, בית שמאי say the יום טבוח is after שבת, and בית הלל say it has no יום טבוח. Doesn't this mean it has no יום טבוח at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה and reads בית הלל as saying that עצרת never gets an extra day for its offerings. That reading would challenge the idea that עצרת has make-up days (תשלומין).
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי do not allow the עולות on יום טוב, so they need a later day to bring them. When עצרת is on Friday, that day gets pushed to after שבת. If בית הלל meant 'no make-up day ever', then an offering missed on עצרת could never be made up, which goes against the view that עצרת has תשלומין.

keyTerms.meaning: The usual name in the משנה for שבועות
'Day of slaughter', the day after the festival when its offerings are brought
'Isn't it that…?', the גמרא suggesting a reading in order to challenge

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: עֲצֶרֶת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: We learned: Shavuot that falls on the eve of Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: יוֹם טְבוֹחַ אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: the day of slaughter is after Shabbat;

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֵין לָהּ יוֹם טְבוֹחַ.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: it has no day of slaughter.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, אֵין לָהּ יוֹם טְבוֹחַ כְּלָל?
phrases.english: What, is it not that it has no day of slaughter at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: עֲצֶרֶת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge from a משנה about עצרת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that עצרת has make-up days (תשלומין) for its offerings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בית הלל say עצרת has 'no יום טבוח' at all, then it cannot have any make-up days.

steps.title: Answer: it just doesn't need one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בית הלל mean עצרת does not need an extra day, not that it can never have one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means it does not need a יום טבוח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge and reads בית הלל's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל allow the עולות on יום טוב itself, so there is no need to wait for a later day. 'אין לה יום טבוח' means 'it does not need one', not 'it is not allowed one'. Make-up days for someone who missed the offering are still possible.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אין לה יום טבוח' sounds like 'there is no such day'. Here it means 'there is no need for such a day', because the offerings can be brought on the festival itself.

phrases.english: No, it means that it does not require a day of slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by reading the משנה's words differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל meant עצרת can never have a later day for its offerings.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל mean only that no later day is needed, since the offerings may be brought on יום טוב itself.

steps.title: Why teach this dispute twice?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה only teaches that the offerings are brought on the festival itself, that is already found in another משנה where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about bringing שלמים and עולות on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does this teach us, that we bring the offerings on the day itself? They already argued about this once! As we learned: בית שמאי say one brings שלמים but does not lean on them, but not עולות. בית הלל say one brings both שלמים and עולות and leans on them.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the עצרת משנה means 'bring the offerings on the day itself', the גמרא asks why it is needed. The same argument already appears in another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other משנה already shows that בית הלל allow עולות on יום טוב and בית שמאי do not. So the עצרת משנה seems to add nothing. The גמרא expects every line of a משנה to teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And what does this teach us?', asking what is new here
That we offer it on its own day
Leaning one's hands on the animal before slaughtering it
Peace-offerings, mostly eaten by the owners
Burnt-offerings, burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: And what does this teach us?
That we offer them on their day?
But they already argued about this once!
As we learned: Beit Shammai say:
One brings peace-offerings but does not lean hands on them;
but not burnt-offerings;

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מְבִיאִין שְׁלָמִים וְעוֹלוֹת
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: one brings peace-offerings and burnt-offerings
and leans hands on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 3 and asks why the משנה would teach it at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the עצרת משנה, now read as 'the offerings are brought on the day itself'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same dispute about bringing עולות on יום טוב already appears in another משנה, so the עצרת משנה would be repeating it.

steps.title: Both teachings are needed
steps.stepSummary: Both משניות are needed. In the regular case בית שמאי may be strict only because the offering can be brought tomorrow. When tomorrow is שבת, we might have thought they agree with בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. If we had only been taught the other case, we would say בית שמאי hold their view there because the offering can be brought the next day. But here, where the next day is שבת, say they agree with בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the dispute has to be taught twice. Each case teaches something the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a normal יום טוב, בית שמאי can be strict because the עולות can wait one day. When עצרת is on Friday, the next day is שבת, so we might think בית שמאי would give in and allow the עולות on יום טוב. The עצרת משנה shows that בית שמאי stay strict and wait until after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is needed', the standard answer that both teachings are necessary
For if it had taught us only…
'I might say', a possible mistaken assumption

steps.whatToRemember: The עצרת משנה is not a repeat. It shows that בית שמאי forbid עולות on יום טוב even when the next day is שבת and the offerings must wait until after שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic צריכא pattern. When a dispute appears twice, the גמרא shows that each case teaches something the other could not.

phrases.english: It is necessary, for had it taught us only this case:
in this case Beit Shammai say their view,
because it is possible to bring it tomorrow.
But here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means עצרת on Friday, when tomorrow is שבת.

phrases.english: I might say they agree with Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by showing both משניות are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the regular יום טוב case alone, we might think בית שמאי are strict only because the עולות can be brought the next day, and would agree with בית הלל when the next day is שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עצרת משנה teaches that בית שמאי stay strict even then and push the offerings to after שבת.

steps.title: The other half of why both משניות are needed
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the משנה about עצרת falling on Friday, we might think בית הלל are lenient only there, and in a regular case they agree with בית שמאי. So both משניות are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught us only that case (עצרת on Friday), we would say: there בית הלל allow it only because the offering cannot be brought tomorrow, which is שבת. But in the regular case, maybe they agree with בית שמאי. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 5 by showing the reverse side: each משנה teaches something the other could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed that the regular משנה alone would not be enough. Here the גמרא shows the Friday משנה alone would not be enough either, because בית הלל's leniency there could come from the special pressure of שבת. Since both teachings are needed, the reading from step 3 holds, and the challenge to עצרת's make-up days is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (both teachings are needed)

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the two משניות teaches something new, so reading 'אין לה יום טבוח' as 'it does not need one' makes sense, and the Friday משנה does not disprove make-up days for עצרת.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only that case,
phrases.notes: "That case" is the משנה about עצרת falling on Friday.

phrases.english: we would say: in that case בית הלל say it
because it is not possible to bring it tomorrow,
phrases.notes: Tomorrow is שבת, when these offerings cannot be brought.

phrases.english: but in this case (a regular יום טוב)
I might say they agree with בית שמאי,
so it is necessary to teach both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכותא begun in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source is needed for a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the Friday משנה, we might think בית הלל agree with בית שמאי on a regular יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both משניות are needed, so the Friday משנה is not extra and does not show anything about make-up days.

steps.title: A proof from a משנה listing the festival days
steps.stepSummary: A source says one who did not celebrate the seven days of פסח, the eight days of סוכות, or the first יום טוב of עצרת can no longer bring the offering. The גמרא suggests this means עצרת has only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who did not bring the festival offering during the seven days of פסח, the eight days of סוכות, or the first יום טוב of עצרת, can no longer bring it. Doesn't this mean the יום טוב of עצרת itself, so there are no make-up days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to answer the open question: does עצרת have make-up days?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For פסח and סוכות the source names all the festival days. For עצרת it names only one day, the יום טוב. That seems to show that once the יום טוב of עצרת passes, the chance is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Celebrated / celebrates, meaning brought the festival offering
The name for שבועות in חז"ל
Doesn't it mean...? Introduces the suggested reading

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָג שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: One who did not celebrate during the seven days of פסח,
phrases.notes: "Celebrate" here means bringing the festival offering.

phrases.english: or the eight days of the festival (סוכות),
or the first יום טוב of עצרת,
can no longer celebrate.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל עֲצֶרֶת!
phrases.english: Doesn't this mean the actual יום טוב of עצרת?!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָג שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the משנה question left open, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That עצרת has no make-up days beyond its one day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source listing the days for bringing the festival offering on each festival.

steps.title: It means the day of slaughter, not the יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the source means the 'day of slaughter' for עצרת, not the יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means the day of slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by reading the source differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the יום טוב of עצרת, the source is talking about the time when the offering may be slaughtered for עצרת. That time can include days after the יום טוב, so the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Day of slaughter: the time set for slaughtering the festival offering

phrases.english: No, it means the day of slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 7 by rereading the words.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The specific reading of 'יום טוב of עצרת' used in the proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase can refer to the day of slaughter, which need not be only the festival day.

steps.title: Then at least it shows there is one day of slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if the source means the day of slaughter, it still says 'day' in the singular, so there would be only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us learn from it that there is only one day of slaughter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 8: even with that reading, the source seems to say there is only one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rereading changed what the day is, but not how many days there are. The source still says one day, which still points to no make-up days.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us resolve the question from it

phrases.english: If so,
let us resolve from it that there is one day of slaughter!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the source means 'day of slaughter'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source uses the singular word, so it still teaches that there is only one day.

steps.title: Read it as 'days of slaughter'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the wording should be read as 'days of slaughter', in the plural.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the reading of the source to the plural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we read 'days of slaughter', the source no longer limits עצרת to one day. So this challenge to עצרת's make-up days falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Say: read the source this way

phrases.english: Say: days of slaughter.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The singular 'day' shows only one day of slaughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'days', so no proof that עצרת has only one day.

steps.title: A proof from comparing עצרת to ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל taught that the Torah says to count days and then make the month holy, and to count days and then make עצרת holy. The גמרא suggests that just as ראש חודש is one day, עצרת is one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבה בר שמואל taught: The Torah said count days and make the month holy, count days and make עצרת holy. Just as the month goes by its count, so עצרת goes by its count. Doesn't this mean we learn from the month: just as ראש חודש is one day, so עצרת is one day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that compares עצרת to ראש חודש, to try to prove that עצרת has only one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ראש חודש and עצרת come after counting days. The ברייתא says each one follows its count. The גמרא tries to read this as: since ראש חודש is one day, עצרת must also be only one day, with no make-up days.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, as רבה בר שמואל taught:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה מְנֵה יָמִים וְקַדֵּשׁ חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: The Torah said: count days and make the month holy,
count days and make עצרת holy.
Just as the month goes according to its count,
so too עצרת goes according to its count.
Doesn't this mean it learns from the month:
just as ראש חודש is one day,
so too עצרת is one day!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, the גמרא tries a second source.
steps.raayaObject: That עצרת is only one day, with no make-up days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבה בר שמואל comparing עצרת to ראש חודש.

steps.title: רבא: עצרת is counted in weeks too
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof. For עצרת we count weeks as well as days, as אביי taught from two פסוקים, and it is even called 'the festival of weeks'. So 'according to its count' means a week, not one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How can you think that? Do we count only days for עצרת and not weeks? אביי said it is a מצוה to count days, as it says 'count fifty days', and a מצוה to count weeks, as it says 'seven weeks you shall count'. And also it is written 'the festival of weeks'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the proof from the ברייתא by showing that עצרת's count is also in weeks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed עצרת is counted only in days, like the month, so it would get one day. רבא shows that the Torah also counts weeks for עצרת and calls it 'חג שבועות'. So 'according to its count' gives עצרת a whole week, which actually supports make-up days.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you think that? Introduces a strong rejection

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove עצרת is one day. Since עצרת is counted in weeks, its 'count' points to a full week of make-up days.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the ברייתא is wrong. He is saying it was read wrongly: 'according to its count' means weeks for עצרת, not one day.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's point removes a proof against make-up days for עצרת. Its 'count' is in weeks, so the comparison to ראש חודש does not limit עצרת to one day.

phrases.english: רבא said: And can you really think that?!
Is that to say that for עצרת we count days
but we don't count weeks?
But didn't אביי say:
It is a מצוה to count days,
as it is written: "You shall count fifty days,"
and it is a מצוה to count weeks,
as it is written: "Seven weeks you shall count for yourself."
And further, it is written: "The festival of weeks."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא given in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that עצרת is one day, like ראש חודש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed עצרת is counted only in days. In fact it is counted in weeks too, so its 'count' means a week.

steps.title: A teaching from the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: proclaiming and reaping
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב links 'you shall proclaim' with 'when you reap'. It concludes that the festival on which you both proclaim and reap is עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught: the Torah says 'And you shall proclaim' and 'when you reap'. Which festival is it on which you both proclaim and reap? It must be עצרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about עצרת. It reads two neighboring פסוקים together to show that עצרת is a festival connected to reaping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proclaiming in the first פסוק belongs to the festival of עצרת. Right after it, the Torah talks about reaping the harvest. Putting the two together tells us there is a festival when you proclaim holiness and can also reap: עצרת. Exactly when that reaping happens is worked out in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say / it must be

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב תָּנָא,
phrases.english: In the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov it was taught:
The verse says: "And you shall proclaim" … "and when you reap."
phrases.notes: These are two words from neighboring פסוקים, ויקרא 23:21 and 23:22, read together.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזֶהוּ חַג שֶׁאַתָּה קוֹרֵא וְקוֹצֵר בּוֹ
phrases.english: Which festival is it on which you both proclaim and reap?
You must say: this is the festival of Atzeret (Shavuot).

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenges to רבי אלעזר's rule were answered, the גמרא brings a further source showing that עצרת has make-up days.
steps.raayaObject: That עצרת has days connected to it on which reaping is done, which leads toward תשלומין.

steps.title: The reaping must be on the make-up days, not on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when this reaping takes place. It cannot be on יום טוב, since reaping is forbidden then. So the source must be talking about the תשלומין days of עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this reaping? If you say on יום טוב itself, is reaping allowed on יום טוב? Rather, it must be talking about the make-up days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It shows that the reaping must happen on the תשלומין days of עצרת, which proves that such days exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reaping is forbidden on יום טוב, so the 'festival when you reap' cannot mean the holiday day itself. The only other option is the make-up days for bringing the festival offerings. These days count as part of the festival, yet they are regular weekdays when reaping is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not…? (leads to the only option left)
Make-up days for bringing missed festival offerings

steps.confusionAlert: 'Is reaping permitted on יום טוב?' is not a real question. It means 'obviously not,' and that forces the reading of תשלומין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a second, independent source that עצרת has תשלומין days.

phrases.english: When?
If you say it means on the Yom Tov itself,
is reaping on Yom Tov permitted?
Rather, is it not referring to the make-up days?
phrases.notes: These are the days after the holiday when someone who missed the festival offerings can still bring them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out when the reaping from step 13 happens, which completes the proof.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, together with the fact that reaping is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: Why רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's source is still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא already had רבי אלעזר's source for תשלומין, so why bring another? From רבי אלעזר alone, we might think work is forbidden on עצרת's make-up days, as it is on the make-up days of פסח. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב teaches that reaping is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though we already have the teaching of רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא, we still need רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's teaching. With only רבי אלעזר's, I would think: just as work is forbidden on the make-up days of פסח, it is also forbidden on the make-up days of עצרת. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why do we need two sources for the same rule? This step explains what the second source adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר learns עצרת's תשלומין by comparing it to פסח. That comparison might carry over פסח's ban on work, because פסח's make-up days are חול המועד. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's source mentions reaping, which shows that work is allowed on עצרת's make-up days.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)

phrases.english: And even though it was already stated,
the teaching that Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya,
the teaching of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov was still needed.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי מִדְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
phrases.english: For if we had only what Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya,
I would have thought:
just as the make-up days of the festival of Matzot (Pesach)
are forbidden for doing work,
so too the make-up days of Atzeret also
are forbidden for doing work.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב.
phrases.english: So the teaching of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיתְּמַר דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא, אִצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the source in steps 13–14 adds something beyond רבי אלעזר's earlier teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that both sources are needed (each teaches something the other does not)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since עצרת's תשלומין are learned from פסח, work would be forbidden on them, as on חול המועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: Work, such as reaping, is allowed on the תשלומין days of עצרת.

steps.title: Starting the other side: what if we had only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins the second half of its explanation. It asks what we would mistakenly think if we had only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had only the teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב…
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to explain why רבי אלעזר's source is also needed, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Showing that two sources are both needed has two sides. Step 15 showed what רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds. Now the גמרא opens the reverse question: what would be missing if we only had his source?

keyTerms.meaning: Showing why each of two sources is needed

phrases.english: And if we had only the teaching of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the reverse half of the explanation begun in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that both sources are needed (second half, continues on the next part of the daf)
